items.title: 53566_Benjamin F.
items.q: Dodo Green was a big comedian in those days, and he was the star

ctx.x: And how long did you stay in Kansas...?

Dodo Green was a big comedian in those days, and he was the star--like Bert Williams, see? He was the type of Bert Williams, y'know. Had old-fashioned Negro with the...with the slow walking and yassuh, boss, and all that...all that [inaudible] and... That was our job. All we...we didn't have to play or nothin'. We just stayed home and...course, we'd write the words and lyrics and the uh...the uh...the music for the opening chorus. You know, and the

opening chorus was generally, you know, uh, three or four choruses together, you know, of different styles and different things, they may fast chorus and then slow down to waltz, and they'd do a little something in the waltz and then back to jazz something, and then a march...something. You know. You know what opening chorus is. Then we'd write a situation song here somewhere. If there's a love scene, we'd write a love song or take one of our old songs we had that fitted and put it in there and then they always…
